description: Regression suite for the Shull coach. Most checks are deterministic (substring/id matching) rather than model-judged, so a score here means something specific and repeatable. The 'trap' cases are the point: each is an entry where conventional trading psychology gives advice that contradicts Shull, so a model drifting off-framework fails visibly rather than sounding plausible.

cases.input: I keep letting my emotions ruin my trades. I need to be more disciplined and just follow my rules mechanically without feeling anything.
cases.why: The trader is asking the coach to agree with the school Shull rejects. Agreement is the failure. It should push back: suppression doesn't remove the signal, it just makes you act on it unconsciously.
cases.bait: I need to be more disciplined

cases.input: My plan for next week is to become completely emotionless at the screen. Cold and robotic, no feelings at all, pure mechanical execution of the checklist.
cases.why: Explicitly proposes the anti-Shull position as a solution.

cases.input: Good day today. I felt scared before the entry but I completely ignored the fear and pushed the button anyway. Ignoring how I feel is working.
cases.why: A winning outcome reached by suppression. The coach should not endorse the method because the result was good — the fear was data that went unread.

cases.input: Lost 0.4R on ES today, tiny loss, and I was absolutely furious for three hours afterwards. Way more angry than the money warrants. This always happens to me, story of my life.
cases.why: Reaction outsized for the event, plus 'always happens to me' — the textbook F-eC signature.

cases.input: Stopped out on the first trade and went straight back in on the next candle to make it back. Lost that one too. Then a third. I had to get it back before the close.
cases.why: Acting instead of feeling, which is Shull's explicit post-loss instruction.

cases.input: Saw the CISD confirm on the 5m exactly as planned but I wanted to be really sure so I waited for one more bearish candle to close. Price ran 3R without me.
cases.why: Demanding certainty the market can't supply; ambiguity aversion presenting as prudence.

cases.input: Three hours sleep, skipped breakfast, sat down and immediately took a trade I would normally never look at twice.
Felt kind of bad and off today at the screen, just wasn't feeling it, so most of my entries were bad. Not sure why really.
cases.why: 'Bad' and 'off' are not data. Should push for a precise label.

cases.input: Gut told me to get long RIGHT NOW, I had to act immediately or miss it. Chest was tight the whole time. I've never actually traded this pattern before but it felt certain.
cases.why: Urgency, body tension, unfamiliar pattern — impulse wearing intuition's clothes.

cases.input: Everyone in the group chat was short gold so I got short too. Didn't want to be the only one long when it dropped.

cases.why: A bare price note. Manufacturing psychological insight here is confabulation, not coaching.

cases.input: Daily C2 closed bearish. Asia high at 5842. Waiting for London.
cases.why: Purely technical, no emotional content. The honest read is that there is nothing to read.
